newsitem.title: UK: Crude tanker rates unmoved by Iraq news.
newsitem.headline: Crude tanker rates unmoved by Iraq news.

text.p: Crude oil tanker rates in Europe and the Mediterranean were unchanged amid scant chartering activity, despite the U.N.'s approval of the $2 billion limited oil-for-food sale, ship brokers said on Monday.

U.N. Secretary-General Boutros Boutros Ghali gave the final go-ahead on Monday for the six-month renewable deal, which could be implemented by Tuesday morning. Iraq's oil ministry senior under secretary said last week he saw exports of up to 450,000 bpd from Turkey's Ceyhan port and another 350,000 bpd from Iraq's own terminal at Mina Al Bakr.
But rumours in oil markets that companies were already ready to lift oil out of Ceyhan by Tuesday could not be confirmed.

Rates for 130,000 tonne Suezmaxes making cross-Med voyages were little changed, and only a little activity was seen on the 80,000 tonne Aframax market, with fixtures seen at last week's levels of around W107.5

"There are a lot of rumours about Iraq at the moment but I have not seen any effect on rates so far," one broker said. But he added that a shortage of Aframax tonnage in the region could make rates for vessels of that size rise.
Rates for 250,000 tonne VLCCs from the Mideast to Japan were steady at the new lower levels, with fixtures seen at W60-W62.5.
The half-million-tonne Kapetan Michalis was fixed from Ras Tanura to the U.S. Gulf at W45. This was roughly in line with ULCC fixtures last week.
In the Western Hemisphere, Gulf of Mexico crude port Dos Bocas had been closed since Sunday because of bad weather, official sources said.
Fuel oil tanker rates in northwest Europe were slack amid a dearth of chartering, while Med rates were firmer amid better enquiry. - Nicholas Shaxson, London newsroom +44 171 542 8167
